tagline: A community-focused financial partner delivering personalized service and innovative solutions.
hero_kpi_rationale: The Net Interest Margin is the primary performance driver for ASB, reflecting the effectiveness of its interest rate management and balance sheet repositioning in a cyclical banking environment.

kpis.name: Net Interest Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between interest income and borrowing costs, expressed as a percentage of earning assets.
kpis.description: The net interest margin increased by 25 basis points in 2025, driven by lower funding costs and the sale of low-yielding assets.
kpis.signal: Margin rising significantly due to lower deposit costs and balance sheet repositioning.

kpis.name: Net Interest Income
kpis.explanation: The bank's primary revenue source from loans and investment securities.
kpis.description: Net interest income increased by $153.9 million in 2025, driven by favorable rate conditions and a repositioning strategy.
kpis.signal: Robust 15% growth due to improved interest rate and balance sheet management.

kpis.name: Provision for Credit Losses
kpis.explanation: Amount set aside to cover potential loan defaults.
kpis.description: Provisions decreased to $54 million in 2025 from $85 million in 2024, reflecting limited portfolio deterioration.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in provisions, indicating stable credit quality.

kpis.name: Noninterest Income
kpis.explanation: Revenue from financial services, capital markets, etc.
kpis.description: Noninterest income more than doubled in 2025, primarily due to non-recurring losses on the sale of mortgage loans and securities.
kpis.signal: Exceptional increase due to non-recurring items related to asset sales.

kpis.name: Noninterest Expense
kpis.explanation: Personnel, advertising, advisory, and other operating costs.
kpis.description: Expenses increased by $37.2 million, driven by variable compensation, healthcare costs, and higher IT spending.
kpis.signal: Increase linked to higher variable compensation and elevated IT expenses.

kpis.short: Return on Average Tangible Common Equity
kpis.name: Return on Average Tangible Common Equity
kpis.explanation: Return generated on average tangible common equity.
kpis.description: ROATCE rose to 13.63% in 2025 from 3.99% in 2024, reflecting strong improvement in profitability.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in ROATCE, indicating improved performance and efficiency.

kpis.name: Efficiency Ratio
kpis.explanation: Ratio of expenses to revenue; lower is better.
kpis.description: The adjusted ratio improved from 59.34% to 56.01%, signaling better cost control.

kpis.name: Average Loans
kpis.explanation: Average loan balance outstanding during the year.
kpis.description: Average loans increased by $892.7 million, driven by commercial and auto lending.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth in commercial and auto loans.

kpis.name: Average Deposits
kpis.explanation: Average deposit balance during the year.
kpis.description: Average deposits increased by $1.5 billion, supported by strong deposit gathering.
kpis.signal: Deposit growth across all segments except short-term accounts.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Increased credit risk in the event of economic recession
risks.score_rationale: Ranked as the top risk factor, with strong language on potential negative impacts on asset quality, loan demand, and earnings. Recession, inflation, and interest rates are repeatedly mentioned. The 2025-2026 context shows heightened vigilance despite current growth. Credit category heavily weighted.

risks.title: Potential inadequacy of the allowance for loan losses
risks.score_rationale: The risk is described as involving a high degree of subjectivity and significant estimation. The text explicitly states that regulators could require an increase, directly affecting capital and earnings. Central placement in the 10-K. Critical Credit category.

risks.title: High concentration in commercial and real estate loans
risks.score_rationale: 65% of the portfolio in commercial loans, including 27% in commercial real estate (CRE), equivalent to 183% of capital. Strong language on high default risk and the impact of one or two non-performing loans. Mention of increased regulatory scrutiny. Priority Credit category.

risks.title: Increased risk related to uninsured deposits
risks.score_rationale: 26.5% of deposits are uninsured ($9.4 billion), with references to bank failures in 2023 and the speed of electronic withdrawals. Mention of heightened federal agency oversight. Prominent placement in the text. Liquidity category significantly impacted.

risks.title: Impact of trade and tariff policies
risks.score_rationale: Mentions tariffs imposed by the Trump administration in 2025, threats of retaliation, and regulatory uncertainty. Effect on customer margins and repayment capacity. Secondary position but concerned tone. Geopolitical category moderately weighted.

risks.title: Reliance on client-provided information
risks.score_rationale: Risk related to the reliability of financial statements provided by borrowers. Impact on credit risk assessment and lending decisions.

ai_positioning.summary: ASB does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
